setter.name: Kim Forbes-Sobers
setter.evidence: so like I told to Kim, I'm pretty seasoned at working out in fitness

prospect.name: Tahseen Chisti
prospect.occupation: Sales team at Treasury Intelligence Solutions, a software company with an IT hub in Sofia
prospect.training_background: Working out consistently for ten to twelve years, seriously for the last five. Trains at home in the mornings, 30-60 minutes depending on wake time. Bodybuilding split — chest day, back day, leg day — mostly on gymnastic rings. Owns kettlebells: two 15s, two 25s, two 35s, one 45 and one 17. Competent on swings and snatches, less sure on cleans. Intermittent fasts noon to eight. Had a personal trainer many years ago.
prospect.medical: Lower back pain during heavy kettlebell snatches — 'I did a workout where I just did like 10 minutes of snatches, and it was fine, but like my lower back was beginning to hurt at some point, so I don't know if my form was wrong, if the weight was too heavy.' History of tennis elbow that he says he needs to manage and strengthen. Limited shoulder mobility in one direction. Hip mobility described as excellent.

signals: Already fit and consistent, wants refinement rather than transformation: 'I'm pretty healthy in terms of my diet anyway, I'm looking for like a fine-tune.'
Explicitly says the programme is priced for someone with more to fix than he has: 'I think your program is more for somebody who needs a lot more than I do.'
Successful and comfortable in a commercial conversation — enterprise software sales, and repeatedly signals he sells for a living.
Divergence from the archetype: price was a real barrier, not a quality signal. He capped at 2 grand and is actively evaluating cheaper competitors.
Signals he will convert if the market validates the price: 'if I do a bunch of others, and everybody's coming around the same price range, then yeah, then it goes from seven and a half to nine.'

goals.text: Grow his legs, which he has always found hardest
Get a kettlebell-focused programme built for him rather than a generic one he could Google
Keep moving as he ages so he does not end up like his parents
Improve shoulder mobility and manage the tennis elbow
Improve cardio and conditioning without hating the sessions
Have a plan that adapts to a 30-minute or a 60-minute morning depending on when he wakes
Have someone counting on him so he stops skipping cardio days
Get form checks so he stops guessing whether he is doing movements correctly

pains.text: Lower back pain during heavy snatch sets and no way to know whether it is form or load
Avoids cardio days out of dread and swaps them for another chest day
Finds kettlebells hard to programme even though he can programme a bodybuilding split easily
Gets wiped out at round five of a ten-round flow, which discourages him
History of tennis elbow he needs to manage
Watched both parents never move, get old and crumble
Discipline slips at weekends and while travelling; just came off a two-week holiday drinking daily
A prior personal trainer was 'just some gym bro' who benched for four days straight

objections.raw_quote: I'll be honest, for someone who knows what I do, think 4K does seem a little high, just between you and I.
objections.rep_response: Accepted the honesty, explained the one-to-one premium via Trevor's demand, then asked whether the future version was worth $4,000.

objections.raw_quote: like I'm pretty healthy in terms of my diet anyway, I'm looking for like a fine-tune, and I think your program is more for somebody who needs a lot more than I do
objections.rep_response: Did not challenge the framing. Moved directly to the community tier and a one-month trial.

objections.raw_quote: With that kind of number, I need to double-track until I talk to my wife, because that's a big number, grand isn't nothing.
objections.rep_response: No response. The rep did not acknowledge it and moved on to the price justification.

objections.raw_quote: Yeah, no, the other programs I've seen were a little less.
objections.rep_response: Positioned as the market leader on price: 'we're higher. probably the highest in price, just honest about that as well.'

objections.raw_quote: and again, I don't, I just, I don't really want to go past three months, I just want to do like a three-month intense workout, see what it, see what it's like
objections.rep_response: Probed the reasoning, agreed with the logic, then quoted a three-month price of $4,000.

offer.payment_plan_terms: No plan structured. Rep said 'Most guys, they put it upfront on a credit card. We do do installments here and there.' Separately offered a one-month entry at $1,200 with $4,800 payable on continuation of a six-month term.
offer.guarantee_mentioned: Only the improvised trial framing: 'you do it for a month, then you're already going to learn a lot. And if you then feel like, well, I actually want to continue... we can continue. If not, we'll just quit it there.' No refund terms stated.

evidence: No decision. He asked for material and time: 'Why don't you send me a follow-up, and then I'll let you know.'
He self-rated 7 to 7.5 out of 10 and told the rep the gap was entirely price: asked whether the missing two and a half points were the price points, he answered 'Yeah, yeah.'
He is running a competitive process: 'I've got some calls scheduled next week with some other trainers' and 'I still have to see what else is out there. Like, I need to do my due diligence.'
He set his own deadline: 'before August, I want to have my decision, so in next two weeks.'
Follow-up agreed for the week of the 27th.
Counter-evidence: he named $2,000 as the range where he could proceed, against a $4,000 three-month price, so the gap is large.
Counter-evidence: the wife consultation was raised and never addressed, so a second decision-maker remains unengaged.
outcome.next_step: Rep to send follow-up material and to reconvene the week of 27 July. Prospect to complete calls with competing trainers and decide before August.

notable.note: Four different prices were quoted on one 42-minute call: $4,000 for three months, $6,000 for six, a $1,200 one-month entry with $4,800 to follow, and the $200 a month community with an unverified claim that it moves to $1,000 per six months 'like, I think next week'. Separately, the prospect said he needed to talk to his wife and the rep did not acknowledge it once — objection play OB has six scripted moves and none ran. Also note the rep told a prospect with disclosed lower back pain during snatches that the self-guided community would be safe because 'you don't have any specific injuries'.
